## On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Status:** Ongoing / unresolved as of last log entry (03:59:27Z) — errors were still increasing in frequency, not self-recovering.

**Root cause:**
Deploy `dep-4471` (gateway, a.novak, 2026-03-14 02:12–02:14Z, "connection-per-request for pool isolation") applied config generation 119, flipping `gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true` (also bumped `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 -> 2500`). This broke connection reuse in the gateway's upstream pool — pool saturates at `in_use=20/20` and never drains, so requests queue and time out with `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED`, surfaced to clients as 503s.

**Impact window:**
- **Start:** 2026-03-14 02:14:18Z — first `503`/`ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED` (`req-07401`, ~4s after dep-4471 finished deploying; first slow-acquire warning at 02:14:14Z).
- **End:** not yet recovered — `waiting` queue on the pool climbed from 13 at first failure to 172+ by 03:55:58Z, with 503s still firing every log cycle at the end of the captured window (03:59Z).
- **Scope:** gateway only. Errors span all four upstreams (billing-svc, orders-svc, catalog-svc, accounts-svc) since it's the shared pool, not one backend. Confirmed via `worker.log` that background job workers were unaffected throughout (normal `db_wait`, no errors) — they don't go through this pool.
- Two later deploys (`dep-4472` billing-svc 02:41Z, `dep-4473` catalog-svc 03:20Z) are unrelated and postdate the onset; not contributors.

**Action: roll back `dep-4471`** (gateway config gen 119) — specifically revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false`. Watch the `pool stats` log line (`in_use`/`waiting`) to confirm the pool drains back to normal (pre-incident baseline was `in_use=5-10`, `waiting=0`).
